items.title: Charged radial equation on subextremal electric RN

references.title: Richard Brito, Vitor Cardoso, and Paolo Pani, Superradiance -- the 2020 Edition, Lecture Notes in Physics 971, second edition
references.locator: Sections 4.1.1 and 4.6.1, equations (4.2a) and (4.55): minimally coupled charged scalar equation and RN separated radial potential. The local sign and mode conventions are taken from the exact Definition above.

references.title: Visakan Balakumar, Aspects of quantum charged scalar field theory in curved spacetime: Black hole superradiance and Hadamard renormalisation, PhD thesis, University of Sheffield (2022)
references.locator: Chapter 3, Sections 3.2.2-3.2.4, equations (3.36)-(3.56): gauge-covariant wave equation, angular separation, charged radial ODE and effective potential. The calculation below is given in the local sign convention.

items.statement:
Let the metric, gauge, parameters, tortoise coordinate, harmonic $Y$, and
operator be exactly those of the charged radial scattering definition. For
$\varpi(r):=\omega-eQ/r$, a smooth separated solution
$\psi=A_{\mathrm{in}}e^{-i\omega t}Y(\Omega)u(r_*)/r$ of
$\Box_{g,A}\psi=0$ has radial function satisfying
$$\frac{d^2u}{dr_*^2}+\left[\left(\omega-\frac{eQ}{r}\right)^2-f(r)\left(\frac{\ell(\ell+1)}{r^2}+\frac{f'(r)}r\right)\right]u=0.$$
Here $f'$ denotes the derivative with respect to $r$, and derivatives of $u$
are with respect to $r_*$.

items.title: Exact charged scattering Wronskian flux identity

references.title: Richard Brito, Vitor Cardoso, and Paolo Pani, Superradiance -- the 2020 Edition, Lecture Notes in Physics 971, second edition
references.locator: Section 4.4, equations (4.50)-(4.53), and Section 4.6.1, equations (4.54)-(4.56): conserved-Wronskian reflectivity identity and charged RN threshold. The local proof includes the long-range Coulomb phase required by the exact $1/r$ tail.

references.title: Visakan Balakumar, Aspects of quantum charged scalar field theory in curved spacetime: Black hole superradiance and Hadamard renormalisation, PhD thesis, University of Sheffield (2022)
references.locator: Chapter 3, Sections 3.3.1-3.3.4, equations (3.76)-(3.84): the four mode boundary conditions and their Wronskian relations, including classical charge superradiance.

items.statement:
Let $u$ be any scattering solution as defined on the fixed subextremal electric
RN exterior, with real $\omega>0$, real $e,Q$, unit incoming amplitude, and
reflection and transmission coefficients $R,T$. Then its radial Wronskian
flux $j:=\operatorname{Im}(\overline u\,\partial_{r_*}u)$ is constant and
$$|R|^2=1-\frac{\omega-eQ/r_+}{\omega}|T|^2.$$
Consequently, if $0<\omega<eQ/r_+$ and $T\ne0$, the reflected radial flux
magnitude exceeds the incident radial flux magnitude, since their ratio is
$|R|^2>1$. This is conditional on an admitted scattering solution and does not
assert its existence, a complex-frequency mode, or a nonlinear instability.
